content.title: About
content.content: Hard plain pretzels are a classic dry snack made from wheat flour, water, yeast and a pinch of salt. They have a crunchy crust and a faintly sweet, baked flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Hard pretzels originated in medieval Europe and were a staple for sailors because they kept well on long voyages.
The traditional twisted shape is said to represent crossed arms in prayer.
In the 19th century the first large‑scale pretzel factories opened in the United States.
Hard pretzels are often used as a base for appetizers, such as cheese dips.
In some countries they are called “Brezel” or “Bretzel.”

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Pretzels provide starch that offers lasting satiety.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Wheat flour supplies a modest amount of iron, important for blood formation.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many snack foods, hard pretzels contain virtually no fat when baked without added oil.

items.title: Provides B‑vitamins
items.content: The dough contributes small amounts of thiamine, niacin and folate.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: The simple composition and lack of heavy additives make them a light snack.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Pretzels can trigger reactions in people with gluten intolerance or wheat allergy.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because of their carbohydrate content, they can raise blood sugar quickly.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Even unsalted versions may contain trace amounts of sodium from processing.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: The hard texture can be a choking risk for young children or individuals with swallowing difficulties.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hard pretzels are convenient as a stand‑alone snack, broken into pieces for salads, soups, or as a crunchy base for cheese sauces. They can also be softened by soaking in milk or yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep them in the refrigerator to prevent mold growth.
